en: The *Āṭavaka-mahāyakṣasenāpati-buddhottara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
Translator unknown;
now appended to the Liang dynasty records.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Rājagṛha in the Kalandakanivāpa of the Bamboo Grove.
At that time, there was a bhikṣu within the city of Rājagṛha.
When they are plundered by bandits, bitten by snakes,
or harassed by ghosts, and thus undergo great suffering and affliction,
at that time the Great General of Ghosts and Spirits, Aṭavaka, [will appear].
Seeing this bhikṣu undergoing such suffering, he felt compassion in his heart.
He immediately went to where the Buddha was, and having arrived,
he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and stood to one side.
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One,
for the sake of subduing all extremely malevolent spirits and ghosts,
and out of my compassion for all sentient beings, I now [make this request]."
In order to subdue all evil spirits and ghosts, as well as all wicked people and malevolent poisons, the Buddha,
the World-Honored One, has bestowed this most formidable and severe incantation to be used for the subjugation of all such spirits and ghosts.
If there are those who read and recite this mantra,
that person’s majesty and virtue, as well as their power, will even be able to subdue Brahmā;
how much more so other evils?
At that time, the Buddha addressed the great general of spirits, Aṭavaka:
"I have no need for this extremely fierce and evil incantation,
which might perhaps cause harm to sentient beings."
At that time, Aṭṭhapada addressed the Buddha once more, saying:
"World-Honored One, in the future evil age,
malevolent spirits will flourish and wicked people will be numerous."
Vicious insects and beasts prey upon sentient beings;
or they encounter various calamities, namely those of kings, thieves, water, fire, weapons,
and the terrors of enmity, hatred, and malevolent spirits.
Whether they be disciples of the Buddha, whether monastic or lay,
whether they be practitioners dwelling in tranquility who subsist on alms,
or those among the fourfold assembly dwelling in cemeteries or at the foot of trees.
Whether traveling through wildernesses, mountain forests, or along roads;
or whether in cities, towns, villages, or streets—
may they be protected and guarded so that they do not encounter evil.
"Blessed One, out of your compassion, we pray that you will graciously accept [this].
Well-Gone One, Blessed One, we pray that you will look upon us with favor.
When the Blessed One heard these words, he accepted them by remaining silent.
At that time, Aṭṭhaka,
seeing that the Buddha remained silent, felt great joy in his heart and immediately spoke this incantation before the Buddha:

World-Honored One, this dharani-phrase serves as protection and salvation for all sentient beings.
They shall protect these people, causing them all to attain peace, tranquility, and stillness;
they shall cause them to be free from decline and affliction, extinguishing all evil poisons,
and liberating them from all suffering and distress— the perils of kings, the perils of bandits, and the perils of enmity and hatred.
If devas, nāgas, ghosts, spirits, rākṣasas, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, āpasmārakas, śīlavartakas, and so forth— those who cause contact and affliction—
[should encounter this, they shall be pacified].
Whatever has been harmed or diminished shall all be eliminated and extinguished.
Furthermore, regarding all poisons in the world— whether from fragrant herbs,
trees, roots, flowers, or fruits— [they shall likewise be neutralized].
May all worldly things— clothing, food, drink,
as well as insects, birds, and beasts capable of being poisonous, malevolent, or harmful to humans—
all be caused to dissolve and perish, so that they can no longer do evil.
Furthermore, regarding the sun, moon, and stars in the void,
or when the whirlwind wind-circles and the spirits and deities raise winds intending to harm people— all such spirits and deities— [are [subdued]].
Those who come seeking food by sucking the vital essence of humans and eating their flesh and blood cause pestilence and fever in people,
lasting for one day, two days, three days, four days, or even up to seven days.
It shall cause all various ailments— whether cold disorders, wind disorders, dampness disorders,
or diseases caused by cold, whether internal or external—
to be completely extinguished within seven days or sixteen days, so that they can no longer inflict harm.
If these various spirits and ghosts— whether with their hands, mouths, feet,
tongues, or minds— should wish to afflict people,
or if wicked persons should wish to cause harm and distress to others;
First, one should recite this mantra, which has the power to silence and restrain them,
causing those evil persons and malevolent spirits to be crushed, lose their mindfulness,
and be unable to commit evil. World-Honored One, I shall now further proclaim a divine mantra to protect them.

This dhāraṇī serves as a protection for those who receive, uphold, read, and recite it.
If there are spirits that consume the vital essence of humans,
or those that damage people's assets and deplete their wealth—
may all such fears, enmities, and the like be completely bound within this boundary.
Now, for the sake of the entire household of [Name] from [Country], I shall provide great protection for immeasurable beings.
Now I shall again recite the incantation for warding off all evils; the incantation is as follows:

At that time, the Great General addressed the Buddha once more, saying:
World-Honored One, this mantra possesses the great spiritual power as described above.
May those who uphold this mantra not have fear of kings,
fear of thieves, fear of fire, or fear of water.
Fear of wind-poisons, weapons, and the like;
fear of the sun, moon, stars, spirits, and deities;
or the occurrence of other evil associates who give rise to resentment in their hearts and harbor malicious intent to cause harm.
If there are those who wish to invade or harass you,
you should first recite this mantra to establish a boundary for them.
This shall cause those evil spirits, wicked people, or enemies whose hearts give rise to malicious intent to desist.
It shall cause them to become deluded, bewildered, and crushed;
encountering these manifold evils, they shall not transcend this realm and shall be unable to harm those who recite this mantra.
World-Honored One, if there are good sons or good daughters who recite this mantra,
all devas, nāgas, asuras, and various evil ghosts and spirits— whether human or non-human— [shall be subdued].
"We shall all attend upon and protect you, ensuring that you do not encounter evil.
World-Honored One, I am a great general of the spirits and ghosts;
my power is sufficient to subdue all malevolent spirits."
If there be anyone who recites this mantra,
I shall lead all the ghosts and spirits to remain by their side day and night,
protecting that person so that they do not behold evil.
I shall not allow evil spirits or wicked people to find any opportunity against them.
If anyone should invade, damage, afflict, or harm those who recite this mantra,
I shall crush their heads with a thousand-spoked wheel.
It causes all ghosts and spirits to bring about decline and harm.
World-Honored One, this mantra possesses supreme spiritual power and supreme majestic virtue.
We only pray that you will bestow it upon the assembly for their peace and happiness.
World-Honored One, as for the power of virtue of one who recites this mantra, only a Buddha knows it.
World-Honored One, this great divine mantra should be entrusted to those who are virtuous, wise, and good.
If one is unable to recite it,
one should write it on fine paper, place it in a multicolored silk pouch,
apply various fragrances to it, and constantly carry it with one's person.
If there should be any sorrow, fear, or peril,
one should always recollect this mantra, and none shall fail to be extinguished.
World-Honored One, if there be any difficulties, sorrows, fears, malevolent spirits, or evil dreams—
If one wishes to cause their destruction,
one should first establish a boundary so that no evils may arise,
causing those evil persons, evil spirits, and evil bandits to suffer the calamity themselves.
The body becomes withered and the mind becomes deranged.
When one wishes to establish the boundary,
one should bathe and purify oneself, put on clean garments, and thoroughly cleanse the ground with pure ointments.
Place seven vessels of various drinks;
two vessels containing a small amount of blood, and two vessels containing various other beverages; then light eight lamps.
Burning incense of *guggulu*, one should offer it with a devoted mind.
I shall lead the various spirits and deities to that person's side to grant their wishes.
That person should recite this mantra, tie a red thread [around their arm], and then carry it with them.
It is able to eliminate all difficulties and calamities.
At that time, the Buddha told Ānanda:
"This mantra possesses exceedingly great supernormal power."
It can eliminate all calamities and the evils of the times,
protecting sentient beings and bringing them great benefit.
You should receive and uphold it well, and cause it to be widely disseminated.
If there are cities, towns, or villages where this mantra is recited, all shall receive its benefits.
If there are kings or ministers who recite this mantra,
their lands and territories will be free from the fear and calamities of wicked bandits.
In the event of calamities, misfortunes, epidemics, floods, droughts, wind, or frost;
or if one encounters wicked bandits, one should recite this mantra.
If it is fastened to the top of a high banner, [it shall bring protection].
Upon seeing this banner, the bandits immediately retreated and were subdued.
Ānanda, this mantra possesses supreme spiritual power and supreme great virtue.
"You should cause the fourfold assembly to skillfully recite and uphold it.
At that time, the assembled multitude, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Regarding this passage, the "Dan" edition contains a commentary which says:
Construct a ritual site using cow dung, with a perimeter of ash and two upright blades; place twelve arrows there.
Invite Bhārgava; the remainder is as before.
Recite the section three times and tie twelve knots in a thread.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Great General of Ghosts and Spirits, Aṭavaka, Spoken by the Buddha.
